title: TestDesiderata
summary: Kent Beck lists properties that make tests valuable and notes some reinforce each other while others, like predictiveness versus speed, trade off.

assertions.quote: Structure-insensitive — tests should not change their result if the structure of the code changes.
Making tests more predictive of production behavior makes them slower.

verdicts.note: Integration and end-to-end tests are consistently slower than unit tests while catching more realistic failures; the test-pyramid literature rests on this.

assertions.quote: Isolated — tests should return the same results regardless of the order in which they are run.

verdicts.note: Flaky-test research at Google and in academia shows order dependence and nondeterminism waste developer time and cause ignored failures.

assertions.quote: Predictive — if the tests all pass, then the code under test should be suitable for production.

verdicts.note: An aspiration; in practice tests cannot cover all production conditions, which is why canaries and monitoring exist.

DORA defines effective automated testing as giving developers confidence that a passing suite means the code can be successfully deployed, and finds such testing predicts CI and CD; this is the report's framing rather than a test of whether suites actually suffice.
